checked.claim: Court read 'and' in Article 53(1)(b) as 'and/or', widening DPO obligation
checked.evidence: Chambers: ruling that the cumulative 'and' should be read as 'and/or', so only one triggering condition is needed. Decided 30 July 2025.
checked.replacement: On 30 July 2025 the Constitutional Court read the cumulative 'and' in the data protection officer trigger (Article 53(1)) as 'and/or', so meeting one condition is enough, widening the DPO obligation.

checked.claim: No body can impose administrative fines; agency fines up to 2% of annual revenue (Article 57; GR 33/2026 Article 185)
checked.evidence: Nusantara: Article 185 GR 33/2026, fine up to 2% of annual revenue; supervisory authority does not yet exist. DLA Piper (updated 13 February 2026): agency not yet operational, draft Presidential Regulation at harmonisation stage.

checked.claim: Law No. 1 of 2026 cut maximum fines to IDR 200 million and IDR 500 million; not confirmed from primary text
checked.evidence: Two independent secondary sources agree. Chambers: fines capped at IDR 200 million (unlawful collection, disclosure, use) and IDR 500 million (forgery), prison terms unchanged. DLA Piper: Law No. 1 of 2026 effective 2 January 2026; collection and use up to 5 years, disclosure 4 years, false data 6 years; corporations up to 10 times.
checked.replacement: Criminal offences cover unlawful collection, disclosure and use of personal data and creating false personal data (Articles 67 and 68), with 4 to 6 years' imprisonment. Law No. 1 of 2026 (penalty adjustment for the new Criminal Code, in force 2 January 2026) cut the maximum fines from IDR 4 to 6 billion to IDR 200 million, or IDR 500 million for false data; corporations face up to ten times the fine plus measures such as licence revocation or dissolution (Article 70).

No body can impose administrative fines; criminal courts do impose penalties (Karanganyar 2023), which fits 'court' better than 'none-yet'.

notes: Most serious: cases[1] dates the DPO Constitutional Court decision to 2024; it was decided 30 July 2025. Law No. 1 of 2026 is now corroborated by two secondary sources (Chambers, DLA Piper) with a 2 January 2026 effective date, so the 'not confirmed' hedge can go; confidence line should be updated accordingly.
